messages.content: my friend asked are you coming home. i do not know whether they mean now or later today.
you can ask which time they mean. for example: do you mean right now, or later today?
why not just answer yes if i will go home later?
yes could make them think you are coming now. if the time is important for what they are asking, a short question can keep the answer clear.
what if i want to answer both at once?
you could say: i am not coming home right now, but i will be home later today.
can you say that without will?
i am not coming home right now, but i plan to be home later today.
does plan to be make the answer sure?
it gives your plan. it does not mean nothing can change it. if you know only that you hope to be home, say that instead.
then use hope. my work may take longer.
i am not coming home right now. i hope to be home later today, but my work may take longer.
now only ask the question about which time.
do you mean right now, or later today?
which is correct: i saw the film or i seen the film?
i saw the film is correct. you can also say i have seen the film, with have before seen.
why not put have before saw?
in this use, have goes with seen, not saw. i have seen the film is correct. i saw the film works without have.
can i say i saw the film yesterday?
yes. that is a clear sentence about when you watched it.
make it about my sister.
my sister saw the film yesterday.
now use seen about her, without yesterday.
my sister has seen the film.
why has instead of have?
use has with my sister in that sentence. with i, you, or they, use have: i have seen it. they have seen it.
can you ask her if she has seen it?
have you seen the film?
why did that question use have if she is my sister?
because you are talking to her as you. the question has you, rather than my sister, so have is correct.
my father was cooking in the other room while i read. i liked hearing him move around.
it sounds like you enjoyed reading while knowing someone was near, without having to talk all the time.
yes. i was alone with the book, but not alone in the house.
those can feel different. you had quiet time with your book and still knew your father was there.
can you make that a sentence i could put with a picture of my book?
i read quietly while my father cooked in the other room, and i liked hearing him there.
i want it less long.
i liked reading with the sound of my father cooking in the other room.
does that say i was helping him cook?
no. it says you were reading and hearing him cook. it does not say that you helped with the food.
now add that i helped after finishing the page.
i read while my father cooked in the other room. after finishing the page, i went to help him.
what did i help with?
you have not said what part you helped with. i should not choose a task unless you want a made up example.
write a story about two friends doing the same reading task in a different way from each other. neither should have to be wrong.

two friends had to read a short story before the next day. one liked to read the whole story first and think about it after. the other liked to stop after each page and write a few words about it. when they talked that evening, they both knew what had happened in the story. one remembered the whole journey of the people, and the other had a page of small details. they used all that information when they talked. they had not read in the same way, but each had found something useful.
why should the story not say one way is always best?
because it only gives these two people and this task. what helps one person may not help another in the same way.
use a shorter explanation with simple words.
both people understood the story. they did not need to do every part in the same way.
what could one ask the other without saying their own way is better?
what helped you remember that part of the story?
make the answer from the person who wrote after each page.
i wrote a few words after each page. looking at them helped me remember the small details.
now answer as the person who read it all first.
i wanted to follow what happened without having to stop after each page. then i thought about the whole story.
finish with them choosing to read together another day.
they chose another story to read later. they would each read in their own way first, then meet to talk about what they found.
i worked for four minutes, had a break for two, then worked for three. how many minutes did i work?
you worked for seven minutes.
how long was it from starting the first part to finishing the last part?
nine minutes, if you add the two minute break to the work time.
can you explain what happened in those nine minutes?
nine minutes: four working, two for a break, and three working again.
why not say i worked for nine minutes?
because two of those minutes were a break. nine is the whole time, while seven is the time you were working.
now i rest for one more minute after finishing the work.
then ten minutes have gone by from the start, but your work time is still seven minutes.
what if i only ask about the time until i finished working?
then the answer is still nine minutes. the last break happened after you finished, so it is outside that part of the time.
only give the time spent on breaks in the whole ten minutes.
three minutes.
now only give the working time.
seven minutes.
my friend said they need more time to answer my question. i can wait. help me reply.
that is okay. take the time you need. i can wait for your answer.
can i say that without making it sound like i have no need for an answer soon?
yes. if you have a time by which you need the answer, say it. if you do not, you can simply say there is no need to answer now.
i do need to know before tomorrow evening.
then you can write: there is no need to answer now, but i need to know before tomorrow evening. would that give you enough time?
what if that is not enough time for them?
then you may need to choose what to do without their answer, or change your own plan if you can. the message gives them a way to tell you the time does not work.
make it less long.
i can wait until tomorrow evening. is that enough time for you?
why ask instead of saying take all the time you need?
because you need the answer before tomorrow evening. asking keeps your reply kind while making that time clear.
use the word before instead of until.
i need your answer before tomorrow evening. is that enough time for you?
a key is in a container on the table. is the key on the table?
the key is inside the container, which is on the table. the more specific place is inside the container. if you want someone to find it, say both.
write that as a short message.
the key is in the container on the table.
now move only the key under the table.
the key is under the table. the container is still on the table.
why not say the container is under the table too?
you asked to move only the key. that does not change the place of the container.
now put the key back inside and move the whole container to the shelf.
the key is in the container on the shelf.
can you know whether the container is open?
no. you gave its place and what is inside, but not whether it is open or closed.
make a question that asks only that.
is the container open?
why is where is the container a different question?
where asks for the place. is the container open asks about whether it is open, rather than where it is.
write a story about someone finding a wrong word in a message before sending it. keep it about a simple visit.

a woman wrote to her brother that she could visit in the morning. she was about to send the message when she remembered that she had work until lunch. she read the sentence again and changed morning to afternoon. then she added a question asking whether that time worked for him. when he answered, they had a plan they could both use. reading the message once more had helped her see that the words did not give the day she really had.
what changed in the message?
she changed the visit from morning to afternoon and asked whether that time worked for her brother.
did her brother have to know her whole work plan?
no. he needed to know when she could visit. the message could give that without every detail of her work.
write the message in her voice.
i can visit in the afternoon, after work. would that time work for you?
what if she is not sure when she will finish work?
then she should leave the time open. she could say: i would like to visit after work, but i do not know when i will finish yet.
make it clear that this is not a sure afternoon plan.
i would like to visit after work. i do not know my finishing time yet, so i cannot give a sure time for the visit.
finish with her finding out before choosing.
she checked her work plan before sending a new time. then she and her brother chose an hour that worked for both.
